messages.subject: Point shape in dataProcessPlotsTMT
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Thank you for building such a user friendly analysis tool! I've been building a TMT labeled data analysis pipeline centered around MSstatsTMT. During this development I largely use the dataProcessPlotsTMT function to generate profilePlots to debug some of the issues I've been running into. One thing that I think could really improve the utility of this function is adding different point shapes for if the point is imputed or not.

To help my own analysis, I changed .plotProfileTMT function in R/dataProcessPlots.R to use the 'censored' column in single_protein as a factor for the point shape. I made these changes by forking the github repository so they can be seen at https://github.com/ekzp6/MSstatsTMT.

Recently I had some very odd results where the log fold change of a particular protein was absurdly negative. When I made the profile plot with this protein, ProfilePlot_29, I saw that there was one non-imputed value (solid circle) that skewed the imputed values (open circles) to be very low. This led to fixing a bug in my TMT purity correction function which generated a much more reasonable log fold change and profile plot, ProfilePlot_31.

I think this small change on the ProfilePlot aesthetics is super heplful and would love to see it in future MSstatsTMT versions.

Thanks,
Emily

Hi,

unfortunately, this is not what I meant.

What you describe is having multiple biological replicates for each conditions, which is not just possible, it's advised and most welcome.

However, to process the data and prepare for group comparison, we need to know which measurements belong to which groups and replicates. Usually, we expect that in each run, each channel corresponds to a single condition (and single biorep. Conversely, single condition may match to multiple channels due to different bioreps). In some processing steps, we assume that for each  Mixture+TechRepMixture, Channel-Condition annotation is the same across all runs (fractions in your case).
However, in your data, this assumption is not true. For run 20210716_ABR_XX_Mix03_Complex, Channel-Condition pairs are different than in other runs. Because of that, one of processing steps fails. If that Channel-Condition annotation is a mistake, it's enough to fix it. If not, we might need to update MSstats code.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

Best K_H.

messages.subject: Re: adjusted p-value calculation in msstats
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dmytro,

I suggest that you compare two analyses step by step, to see where the differences arise. In principle, every step can be affected by adding one more run. In particular, very early in the process there are filters, such as 'remove features with too many missing values'. When an extra run is added these filters may keep more proteins, and a larger protein number affects the multiple testing correction (more proteins require more conservative decisions). I do not know how many replicates you have, but this will be particularly the case in studies with a small number of runs. This said, if the number of runs is small, I am surprised that adding a new run does not change the log2FC and the p-values.

So in short, please compare the results at each step, starting from filtering and normalization. Hopefully it will help you clarify where exactly the difference occurs.

Thank you for using MSstats

Sincerely
Olga
